questions.q: What is the change from gas to liquid called?
questions.why: Condensation is a gas turning into a liquid as it cools.

questions.q: Which gas diffuses fastest at the same temperature?
questions.why: Lighter molecules move faster on average, so the gas with the lowest Mr diffuses fastest.

questions.q: A substance melts at −7 °C and boils at 59 °C. What state is it at 25 °C?
questions.why: 25 °C is above its melting point and below its boiling point.

questions.q: An atom of sodium has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its nucleon (mass) number?
questions.why: Nucleon number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23.

questions.q: What is the electronic configuration of chlorine (proton number 17)?
questions.why: Shells fill 2, then 8, then the remaining 7.

questions.q: What type of bonding is in sodium chloride?
questions.why: Electrons transfer from sodium to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held by electrostatic attraction.

questions.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity?
o: Each carbon has one delocalised electron that can move
questions.why: Each carbon bonds to three others, leaving one electron free to move between the layers.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting points?
o: The forces between molecules are weak
questions.why: Melting overcomes the weak intermolecular forces, not the strong covalent bonds inside molecules.

questions.q: What is the relative formula mass of CO₂? (C = 12, O = 16)
How many moles are in 36 g of water? (Mr = 18)
questions.why: moles = mass ÷ Mr = 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

questions.q: What volume does 0.5 mol of any gas occupy at room temperature and pressure? (molar volume 24 dm³)
25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ NaOH is neutralised. How many moles of NaOH are there?
questions.why: moles = concentration × volume in dm³ = 0.100 × 0.0250 = 0.00250.

questions.q: Which is the balanced equation for magnesium burning?
questions.why: Two Mg and two O on each side.

questions.q: What is the relative formula mass of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂? (Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some ignored the brackets and worked out 'MgOH₂'. 24 + 2 × (16 + 1) = 58.

long.q: Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of calcium oxide made from 25 g of calcium carbonate. (Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
scheme: M1: Mr(CaCO₃) = 100, so moles = 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25
M1: moles of CaO = 0.25 (1 : 1)

questions.q: In electrolysis, what forms at the cathode when molten lead(II) bromide is electrolysed?
questions.why: Positive Pb²⁺ ions go to the negative cathode and gain electrons to form lead.

questions.q: Why must ionic compounds be molten or dissolved to be electrolysed?
o: So the ions are free to move
So electrons can move through them
questions.why: In a solid the ions are fixed; they must be free to move to carry the current.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride, what forms at the anode?
questions.why: With concentrated chloride, chloride ions are discharged at the anode as chlorine.

questions.q: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell, what is the only product?
questions.why: Hydrogen and oxygen combine to form water, releasing electrical energy.

questions.q: Which are the inputs to a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): most candidates thought hydrogen and oxygen were outputs. They are the fuels; water and electrical energy come out.

questions.q: What forms at the cathode when concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): a common error was 2H instead of H₂. Hydrogen is diatomic; sodium is too reactive to be discharged from water.

long.q: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed using inert electrodes. Name the products at each electrode and write the ionic half-equation at the cathode.
scheme: B1: anode (positive): chlorine
B1: cathode (negative): hydrogen
B1: the solution left contains sodium hydroxide

questions.q: In an exothermic reaction, the temperature of the surroundings…
questions.why: Exothermic reactions transfer thermal energy to the surroundings.

questions.q: Bond breaking is…
questions.why: Energy must be taken in to break bonds; making bonds releases energy.

questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = −90 kJ/mol. It is…
questions.why: A negative ΔH means energy is released to the surroundings.

questions.q: Which change increases the rate of a reaction between marble chips and acid?
questions.why: Powder has a larger surface area, giving more frequent collisions.

questions.q: What does a catalyst do?
o: It is used up in the reaction
It increases the rate without being used up
questions.why: A catalyst provides a route with lower activation energy and is unchanged at the end.

questions.q: In the Haber process, what is made?
questions.why: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, using an iron catalyst.

questions.q: Oxidation is…
questions.why: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss of electrons, reduction is gain.

questions.q: For an equilibrium, increasing the pressure shifts the position towards…
o: the side with more moles of gas
the side with fewer moles of gas
questions.why: The equilibrium shifts to reduce the pressure, towards fewer gas molecules.

questions.q: In the Contact process, which conditions are used?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many confused the Contact process with the Haber process (iron catalyst, 20 000 kPa).

long.q: Use collision theory to explain why increasing the concentration of an acid increases the rate of its reaction with magnesium.
scheme: B1: more acid particles in the same volume
B1: so more frequent collisions between particles
B1: more successful collisions per second

questions.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25 °C?
questions.why: pH 7 is neutral; below is acidic, above is alkaline.

questions.q: Which ion is present in all acidic solutions?
questions.why: Acids release hydrogen ions in water.

questions.q: Acid + metal carbonate gives a salt, water and…
questions.why: Carbonates fizz with acids, releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which salt is insoluble in water?
questions.why: Most sulfates dissolve, but barium, calcium and lead sulfates don't.

questions.q: How is an insoluble salt made?
questions.why: Mixing two soluble salts that swap ions forms the insoluble salt as a precipitate.

questions.q: A salt is made by adding excess copper(II) carbonate to dilute sulfuric acid. What is the next step?
o: Filter to remove the excess copper(II) carbonate
Add more acid until it fizzes again
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many crystallised before removing the excess solid. Filter first, then heat the filtrate to the crystallising point.

long.q: Describe how to prepare pure, dry crystals of copper(II) sulfate from copper(II) oxide and dilute sulfuric acid.
scheme: B1: warm the acid and add copper(II) oxide until some is left over (excess)
B1: filter to remove the excess copper(II) oxide
B1: heat the filtrate to evaporate some water, to the point of crystallisation
B1: leave to cool so crystals form
B1: filter off the crystals and dry them between filter papers

questions.q: Group 1 metals become more reactive down the group because…
o: the outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily
they have more protons attracting the electron
questions.why: Shielding and distance make the single outer electron easier to lose.

questions.q: Which halogen is a dark grey solid at room temperature?
questions.why: Iodine is a grey-black solid; chlorine is a gas and bromine a red-brown liquid.

questions.q: Chlorine is bubbled into potassium bromide solution. What happens?
o: Bromine is displaced and the solution turns orange
questions.why: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from its salts.

questions.q: Why are the noble gases unreactive?
o: They have full outer shells of electrons
questions.why: A full outer shell is stable, so they don't need to gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.q: Elements in the same group have the same number of…
questions.why: The group number (for groups 1 to 7) is the number of outer electrons.

questions.q: What is the state of bromine at room temperature and pressure?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): a common misconception is that bromine is a gas. It is a red-brown liquid that gives off a vapour.

long.q: Explain why the Group I metals become more reactive down the group.
scheme: B1: the atoms get larger, with more electron shells
B1: so the outer electron is further from the nucleus / more shielded, less strongly attracted
B1: so it is lost more easily

questions.q: Which metal is extracted from its ore by electrolysis, not by carbon?
questions.why: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so it is extracted by electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide.

questions.q: Why are alloys often harder than pure metals?
o: Different-sized atoms disrupt the layers so they can't slide easily
questions.why: Atoms of a different size stop the layers sliding over one another.

questions.q: What two things are needed for iron to rust?
questions.why: Rusting needs both oxygen (air) and water.

questions.q: Galvanising protects iron by coating it with…
questions.why: Zinc is more reactive and corrodes in place of the iron (sacrificial protection).

questions.q: Which metal does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many did not recall that copper does not react with dilute acids; it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

questions.q: Which gas from car engines causes acid rain?
questions.why: Nitrogen oxides (and sulfur dioxide) dissolve in rain to form acids.

questions.q: What is the main gas in clean dry air?
questions.why: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.q: Which two gases are greenhouse gases?
questions.why: Carbon dioxide and methane absorb and re-emit infrared radiation.

questions.q: Why is chlorine added to drinking water?
questions.why: Chlorine kills bacteria in water treatment.

questions.q: How does methane add to the enhanced greenhouse effect?
o: It absorbs thermal energy emitted by the Earth and re-emits some back towards the Earth
It reflects sunlight back to space
questions.why: Examiners (2023): answers often confused the greenhouse effect with ozone or acid rain.

questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
questions.why: Alkanes are saturated: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, e.g. methane CH₄.

questions.q: Which test shows a compound is unsaturated?
o: Bromine water turns from orange to colourless
questions.why: Alkenes add across the C=C double bond, decolourising bromine water.

questions.q: What is the main use of fractional distillation of petroleum?
o: To separate it into fractions with different boiling ranges
questions.why: Fractions condense at different heights of the column according to boiling range.

questions.q: Ethanol can be made by fermentation of…
questions.why: Yeast converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide, around 25–35 °C, without oxygen.

questions.q: What type of polymerisation makes poly(ethene)?
questions.why: Ethene molecules add together by opening their double bonds; nothing else is formed.

questions.q: What type of reaction happens when ethene reacts with bromine?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many did not recall this. Bromine adds across the C=C bond, which is why the orange colour disappears.

long.q: Ethene can be made into poly(ethene). Name this type of polymerisation and describe a test that shows ethene is unsaturated.
scheme: B1: addition polymerisation
B1: add bromine water
B1: it changes from orange to colourless

questions.q: In chromatography, how is the Rf value worked out?
o: distance moved by solvent ÷ distance moved by spot
distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent
questions.why: Rf = distance travelled by the substance ÷ distance travelled by the solvent front.

questions.q: How would you separate salt from salt solution?
questions.why: Evaporating the water leaves the salt crystals behind.

questions.q: Which gas turns limewater milky?
questions.why: CO₂ forms insoluble calcium carbonate with limewater.

questions.q: A flame test gives a lilac flame. Which ion is present?
questions.why: Potassium gives lilac; sodium yellow, lithium red, calcium orange-red.

questions.q: Adding aqueous sodium hydroxide gives a light blue precipitate. Which ion?
questions.why: Copper(II) hydroxide is light blue; iron(II) is green and iron(III) red-brown.

questions.q: Which test identifies chlorine gas?
o: Add acidified silver nitrate: white precipitate
Damp blue litmus paper turns red then is bleached
A lighted splint gives a squeaky pop
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the test for chlorine gas was often confused with the test for chloride ions (silver nitrate).
